pathway.title: ESCO TECHNOLOGIES INC — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: ESCO has very low reported leverage and strong cover. Total borrowings were USD 85.0 million at June 30, 2026, down from USD 186.0 million at September 30, 2025, so total debt to EBITDA fell from 0.758x to 0.278x and net debt to EBITDA from 0.345x to 0.038x. EBITDA covered cash interest paid 20.42x on an LTM basis against 14.09x for FY2025 [CP-1 Chart data]. The mechanism was operating cash flow from continuing operations of USD 193.377 million in nine months 2026 funding net repayment and other uses, so the debt reduction came from cash generation, which supports debt service capacity [CP-1 Narrative review: leverage].

ESCO has ample liquidity and a short near-term maturity profile. Cash was USD 73.236 million and the revolver had USD 442.300 million undrawn after USD 12.7 million of letters of credit, together USD 515.536 million; USD 20.000 million of term loan A is current and USD 65.000 million falls due by August 30, 2028, which is the maturity of the existing revolver and term loan A [CP-1 Chart data]. The existing facility is secured by guarantees from material US subsidiaries and a pledge of equity of material foreign subsidiaries [CP-1 Debt instruments and facilities]. Because the facility is to be replaced at the Megger closing, this maturity profile is a pre-closing picture. The wording of the current portion changed from voluntary in Q1 2026 to obligated in Q2 and Q3 2026, a logged conflict the supplied documents do not explain [CP-1A Conflicts].

ESCO has diversified operations with a government-weighted core. Aerospace & Defense was approximately 44% of fiscal 2025 revenue, Utility Solutions Group approximately 35% and RF Test approximately 21%; the US Government and its contractors were approximately 23%, and no customer exceeded 10% [CP-1A Company and operating model]. Backlog of USD 1,540.5 million, with approximately 59% expected in the next twelve months, gives revenue visibility, but Government contracts are terminable for convenience and fixed-price contracts expose margins to cost overruns [CP-1A Credit translations].

ESCO's cash flow in the latest nine months may overstate a normal level. Continuing operating cash flow of USD 193.377 million benefited from customer advances, with contract liabilities up USD 71.5 million, and discontinued operations used USD 59.340 million, alongside approximately USD 59 million of cash tax paid on the VACCO gain. LTM free cash flow of USD 258.102 million is therefore a continuing-operations figure before that one-time outflow and before dividends [CP-1 Narrative review: cash flow quality]. Customer advances can reverse as projects deliver, which would lower operating cash flow.

ESCO's acquisition will change the credit. The Megger purchase has total consideration of approximately USD 2.35 billion, of which USD 0.9 billion is cash and approximately USD 1.4 billion is ESCO equity, with closing expected in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 [CP-1A Transaction summary]. Committed financing is a new senior secured revolver, term loan A and term loan B of USD 500 million each, effective only at closing and replacing the existing facility [CP-1 Debt instruments and facilities]. Megger's financials are not supplied, so post-closing leverage and cover are not calculable. As a bound only, CP-1 shows that if the full USD 0.9 billion cash consideration were borrowed on top of current debt, total debt would be about 3.22x ESCO-only LTM EBITDA before Megger earnings; this is an Analyst Inference, not a forecast [CP-1 Narrative review: leverage]. The 2026-11-05 as-of date falls after the start of the expected closing quarter, and nothing after August 10, 2026 is supplied, so closing status is unknown.

ESCO's covenants cannot be tested. The existing facility has a leverage ratio and an interest coverage ratio, and management reported compliance at June 30, 2026, but levels, definitions and the reported ratios are not supplied, and the New Credit Facility terms are not supplied [CP-1 Covenants and definitions]. Headroom is therefore not calculable, and the reported ratios in this credit view are not covenant ratios.

ESCO's observed conduct supports creditors, and ownership will change. VACCO proceeds were used mainly to pay down debt, dividends are small, there were no buybacks in fiscal 2025 or Q3 2026 and no creditor-adverse action appears in the supplied sources. TBG AG will receive ESCO shares and sign a shareholder agreement at completion; its stake, governance rights and lock-up terms are not supplied [CP-1A Ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour].

runs.text: ESCO's strengths start with its balance sheet. Reported leverage is low (total debt to EBITDA 0.278x) and cash interest cover is high (20.42x) on LTM figures, giving the issuer capacity to absorb a cost or volume shock before the acquisition financing [CP-1 Chart data; Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation]. Liquidity of USD 515.536 million is dominated by an undrawn revolver that matures August 30, 2028, so near-term refinancing risk is low [CP-1 Chart data; Documentary Fact]. Backlog of USD 1,540.5 million and a three-segment mix with no customer above 10% of sales support revenue visibility and limit single-customer risk [CP-1A Company and operating model; Documentary Fact]. Capital allocation since fiscal 2025 has favoured creditors, with debt repaid from divestiture proceeds, small dividends and no buybacks [CP-1A Ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour; Documentary Fact]. Cash generation from continuing operations was strong in the latest period [CP-1 Narrative review; Documentary Fact, qualified by working capital timing].

ESCO's weaknesses concentrate on the pending transaction and on missing documents. The Megger purchase is large relative to the existing debt, is funded partly with new term debt, and its terms and Megger's earnings are not supplied, so the leverage that creditors will face is unknown [CP-1A Transaction summary; Insufficient Information, with the missing datapoints being the credit agreement, Megger financials and closing status]. Covenant levels and headroom are missing for both the existing and the new facility [CP-1 Covenants and definitions; Insufficient Information]. Government funding concentration in Aerospace & Defense, termination for convenience and fixed-price cost risk could affect the largest and fastest-growing segment [CP-1A Credit translations; Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation]. Operating cash flow was lifted by customer advances and the reported free cash flow excludes a discontinued-operations outflow, so cash conversion is flattered in the nine months [CP-1 Narrative review: cash flow quality; Analyst Interpretation]. TBG AG's resulting stake and governance rights are unknown, which limits the view of control and alignment after closing [CP-1A Ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour; Insufficient Information]. Smaller weaknesses are renewables exposure in the utility segment, sole-source suppliers, and internal-control scope that excludes recently acquired businesses until they are tested [CP-1A Company and operating model; Documentary Fact].

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The pending transaction is the acquisition of Megger Group Limited from TBG AG. On April 15, 2026 ESCO signed a definitive agreement: 10-Q Q3 page:19 states "ESCO will acquire Megger for total consideration of approximately $2.35 billion, consisting of $0.9 billion in cash and ESCO equity valued at approximately $1.4 billion." The agreement is a share purchase agreement (10-Q Q3 page:30 "for the sale and purchase of the share capital of Megger Group Limited") with a Form of Shareholder Agreement to be executed concurrently with completion. The cash and equity components are each stated as approximate and do not sum to the stated total; the filing does not explain the difference, and it is logged below, not reconciled.

Status and timing. The transaction was signed after the March 31, 2026 balance sheet date and was reported as a "Subsequent Event" in the 10-Q Q2 (page:24). Management states that "All filings for regulatory approval are underway" and expects closing in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 (Release Q3 page:3 and 10-Q Q3 page:19). Whether approvals were received and whether it has closed by 2026-11-05 is Not supplied.

Financing and new debt. The cash portion "will be funded through existing cash on hand and incremental debt, with committed financing in place" (10-Q Q3 page:19). On May 29, 2026 ESCO and certain subsidiaries entered into a Credit Agreement, the New Credit Facility, with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as administrative agent. It provides a senior secured revolving credit facility of $500 million, a senior secured term loan A of $500 million and a senior secured term loan B of $500 million. It becomes effective only on, and substantially concurrently with, closing and replaces the Existing Credit Facility. The revolver and term loan A mature five years after the effective date and term loan B seven years after (10-Q Q3 page:12). Foreign subsidiaries may also draw. No notes, bonds or other capital-markets debt issue is described in any supplied source. The credit agreement is Exhibit 10.3 to the 10-Q Q3 and was filed with the Form 8-K of June 3, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:30); it is not in the pack, so pricing, covenants, conditions to effectiveness, guarantors and collateral are Not supplied.

Ownership effect. The equity component means ESCO will issue shares to TBG AG at completion. The number of shares, the resulting percentage ownership, lock-up terms, board or consent rights and any standstill under the shareholder agreement are all Not supplied. No percentage is inferred here.

Use of proceeds and liquidity effect. Proceeds fund the purchase price; fees, expenses and any refinancing of the Existing Credit Facility are not itemised in the supplied sources. CP-1 shows $85.0 million of borrowings and $73.2 million of cash at June 30, 2026 before the transaction, and an illustrative bound of 3.22x on ESCO-only EBITDA if the full $0.9 billion were borrowed (CP-1, Analyst Inference, not a forecast). Megger financials are Not supplied, so the actual pro forma leverage and liquidity cannot be stated.

Costs already incurred. Approximately $7 million of debt financing costs were expensed in Q3 2026 interest expense (10-Q Q3 page:23), and acquisition costs at Corporate are excluded from adjusted EPS (Release Q3 page:6 "$0.20 of debt financing and $0.19 of acquisition costs"). These are Documentary Fact; they show the financing was committed before the 10-Q Q3 period end.

Creditor mechanics. A large acquisition funded partly by new term debt replaces an $85.0 million drawn facility with up to $1.5 billion of committed capacity (three tranches of $500 million, see Calculations). The creditor question is leverage tolerance, covenant terms and the term loan B tenor. Willingness is evidenced by the committed financing and the signed agreement; legal capacity (what the new agreement permits) and feasibility (post-closing cash flow of the combined group) are not shown.

Earlier financing for context: the Maritime acquisition in April 2025 for a cash purchase price of approximately $472 million, net of cash acquired (10-K page:74), was partly funded by the Incremental Facility (10-K page:80), which is the term loan A now outstanding.

fields.value: ESCO is a publicly listed group with no sponsor or parent named in the context or the filings; material US subsidiaries guarantee the bank facility (10-K page:80). It reports three segments: Aerospace & Defense (A&D), Utility Solutions Group (USG) and RF Test & Measurement (Test). A&D has grown from 34% of continuing revenue in 2023 to 44% in 2025, reflecting Navy growth and the Maritime acquisition, which makes the group more dependent on US and UK naval programs and on government funding. The group sold its Space business (VACCO) in July 2025 and used the proceeds mainly to repay debt, so fiscal 2025 and the first nine months of fiscal 2026 show deleveraging rather than distributions.

fields.value: The transaction that matters is the pending purchase of Megger Group Limited from TBG AG, signed April 15, 2026, with total consideration of approximately $2.35 billion, of which approximately $0.9 billion is cash and approximately $1.4 billion is ESCO equity. Megger, which the 10-K lists as a competitor of the USG segment, will join USG. The cash part is to be funded from cash and incremental debt, with a new $1.5 billion committed facility set agreed on May 29, 2026 that is effective only on closing. Closing was expected in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, which began October 1, 2026, so by the 2026-11-05 as-of date the transaction may have closed. fields.value: ESCO TECHNOLOGIES INC (issuer id `ese`) is assessed as of 2026-11-05 on the `credit_snapshot` pathway. The scope is the fundamental credit view built only from the CP-0, CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs, with no source text re-read and no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CP-2 works from upstream handoffs only. The issuer sources below are the files those handoffs rely on; this module did not reopen them, and every figure and fact here traces to CP-1 or CP-1A.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Bracketed basis labels name the upstream section: CP-1 sections are "Chart data", "Financials and credit metrics", "Debt instruments and facilities", "Claims outside debt", "Covenants and definitions" and "Narrative review"; CP-1A sections are "Company and operating model", "Company profile", "Transaction summary and new debt issues", "Ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour", "Timeline", "Conflicts and document differences" and "Credit translations". Periods follow the fiscal year ending September 30: Q3 2026 is the quarter ended June 30, 2026, LTM is the twelve months to June 30, 2026. Currency is USD.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: ESCO Technologies currently has a strong, lightly levered credit profile, but the credit view depends on a pending acquisition that this evidence cannot size. At June 30, 2026 ESCO had USD 85.0 million of borrowings against LTM EBITDA of USD 305.677 million (total debt 0.278x, net debt 0.038x), liquidity of USD 515.536 million and backlog of USD 1,540.5 million [CP-1; CP-1A Company and operating model]. The weakest point is that this describes ESCO before the Megger purchase, which includes USD 0.9 billion of cash funded under new facilities whose terms, and Megger's own earnings, are not supplied [CP-1A Transaction summary]. What decides the outcome is whether closing has occurred, how much is drawn on the new term loans and what the covenants allow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Confidence is Medium, not High, because CP-1A judged CP-2 ready only with limitations (see Gaps) and the covenant and transaction documents are missing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: ESCO has very low reported leverage and strong cover. Total borrowings were USD 85.0 million at June 30, 2026, down from USD 186.0 million at September 30, 2025, so total debt to EBITDA fell from 0.758x to 0.278x and net debt to EBITDA from 0.345x to 0.038x. EBITDA covered cash interest paid 20.42x on an LTM basis against 14.09x for FY2025 [CP-1 Chart data]. The mechanism was operating cash flow from continuing operations of USD 193.377 million in nine months 2026 funding net repayment and other uses, so the debt reduction came from cash generation, which supports debt service capacity [CP-1 Narrative review: leverage].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: ESCO has ample liquidity and a short near-term maturity profile. Cash was USD 73.236 million and the revolver had USD 442.300 million undrawn after USD 12.7 million of letters of credit, together USD 515.536 million; USD 20.000 million of term loan A is current and USD 65.000 million falls due by August 30, 2028, which is the maturity of the existing revolver and term loan A [CP-1 Chart data]. The existing facility is secured by guarantees from material US subsidiaries and a pledge of equity of material foreign subsidiaries [CP-1 Debt instruments and facilities]. Because the facility is to be replaced at the Megger closing, this maturity profile is a pre-closing picture. The wording of the current portion changed from voluntary in Q1 2026 to obligated in Q2 and Q3 2026, a logged conflict the supplied documents do not explain [CP-1A Conflicts].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: ESCO has diversified operations with a government-weighted core. Aerospace & Defense was approximately 44% of fiscal 2025 revenue, Utility Solutions Group approximately 35% and RF Test approximately 21%; the US Government and its contractors were approximately 23%, and no customer exceeded 10% [CP-1A Company and operating model]. Backlog of USD 1,540.5 million, with approximately 59% expected in the next twelve months, gives revenue visibility, but Government contracts are terminable for convenience and fixed-price contracts expose margins to cost overruns [CP-1A Credit translations].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: ESCO's cash flow in the latest nine months may overstate a normal level. Continuing operating cash flow of USD 193.377 million benefited from customer advances, with contract liabilities up USD 71.5 million, and discontinued operations used USD 59.340 million, alongside approximately USD 59 million of cash tax paid on the VACCO gain. LTM free cash flow of USD 258.102 million is therefore a continuing-operations figure before that one-time outflow and before dividends [CP-1 Narrative review: cash flow quality]. Customer advances can reverse as projects deliver, which would lower operating cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: ESCO's acquisition will change the credit. The Megger purchase has total consideration of approximately USD 2.35 billion, of which USD 0.9 billion is cash and approximately USD 1.4 billion is ESCO equity, with closing expected in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 [CP-1A Transaction summary]. Committed financing is a new senior secured revolver, term loan A and term loan B of USD 500 million each, effective only at closing and replacing the existing facility [CP-1 Debt instruments and facilities]. Megger's financials are not supplied, so post-closing leverage and cover are not calculable. As a bound only, CP-1 shows that if the full USD 0.9 billion cash consideration were borrowed on top of current debt, total debt would be about 3.22x ESCO-only LTM EBITDA before Megger earnings; this is an Analyst Inference, not a forecast [CP-1 Narrative review: leverage]. The 2026-11-05 as-of date falls after the start of the expected closing quarter, and nothing after August 10, 2026 is supplied, so closing status is unknown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: ESCO's covenants cannot be tested. The existing facility has a leverage ratio and an interest coverage ratio, and management reported compliance at June 30, 2026, but levels, definitions and the reported ratios are not supplied, and the New Credit Facility terms are not supplied [CP-1 Covenants and definitions]. Headroom is therefore not calculable, and the reported ratios in this credit view are not covenant ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: ESCO's observed conduct supports creditors, and ownership will change. VACCO proceeds were used mainly to pay down debt, dividends are small, there were no buybacks in fiscal 2025 or Q3 2026 and no creditor-adverse action appears in the supplied sources. TBG AG will receive ESCO shares and sign a shareholder agreement at completion; its stake, governance rights and lock-up terms are not supplied [CP-1A Ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: ESCO's strengths start with its balance sheet. Reported leverage is low (total debt to EBITDA 0.278x) and cash interest cover is high (20.42x) on LTM figures, giving the issuer capacity to absorb a cost or volume shock before the acquisition financing [CP-1 Chart data; Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation]. Liquidity of USD 515.536 million is dominated by an undrawn revolver that matures August 30, 2028, so near-term refinancing risk is low [CP-1 Chart data; Documentary Fact]. Backlog of USD 1,540.5 million and a three-segment mix with no customer above 10% of sales support revenue visibility and limit single-customer risk [CP-1A Company and operating model; Documentary Fact]. Capital allocation since fiscal 2025 has favoured creditors, with debt repaid from divestiture proceeds, small dividends and no buybacks [CP-1A Ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour; Documentary Fact]. Cash generation from continuing operations was strong in the latest period [CP-1 Narrative review; Documentary Fact, qualified by working capital timing].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: ESCO's weaknesses concentrate on the pending transaction and on missing documents. The Megger purchase is large relative to the existing debt, is funded partly with new term debt, and its terms and Megger's earnings are not supplied, so the leverage that creditors will face is unknown [CP-1A Transaction summary; Insufficient Information, with the missing datapoints being the credit agreement, Megger financials and closing status]. Covenant levels and headroom are missing for both the existing and the new facility [CP-1 Covenants and definitions; Insufficient Information]. Government funding concentration in Aerospace & Defense, termination for convenience and fixed-price cost risk could affect the largest and fastest-growing segment [CP-1A Credit translations; Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation]. Operating cash flow was lifted by customer advances and the reported free cash flow excludes a discontinued-operations outflow, so cash conversion is flattered in the nine months [CP-1 Narrative review: cash flow quality; Analyst Interpretation]. TBG AG's resulting stake and governance rights are unknown, which limits the view of control and alignment after closing [CP-1A Ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour; Insufficient Information]. Smaller weaknesses are renewables exposure in the utility segment, sole-source suppliers, and internal-control scope that excludes recently acquired businesses until they are tested [CP-1A Company and operating model; Documentary Fact].
